page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 480 MB of shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions including Intel AMX (tile and int8) alongside AVX-512 vector instruction sets. The server includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation.

Hardware benchmark testing shows strong throughput in selected execution profiles, including static web serving throughput measuring 43.89 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 35.62 GB/sec. In quantized small and medium language model workloads, CPU-based prompt processing and generation reach top-quartile performance bands due to AMX and AVX-512 extensions. Memory bandwidth reaches 181.75 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 2352.2 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read blocks, while multi-core stress-ng tests and PassMark CPU metrics sit within median performance distributions.

The server does not include local NVMe or ephemeral disk storage, requiring external Azure Premium Storage attachments for persistent file systems. It also lacks discrete GPU hardware. Cost efficiency is driven by its high memory-to-vCPU density and substantial L3 cache allocation, which allow organizations to consolidate memory-bound enterprise systems onto fewer virtualized nodes without paying for unneeded hardware accelerators.

Microsoft Azure E32s_v7 is designed for in-memory databases, large caching layers such as Redis, enterprise relational database systems, memory-intensive batch processing, and CPU-driven inference workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E32s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes 480 MB of L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 instruction support. It is provisioned with 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, with no onboard local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Synthetic and application testing shows strong capabilities in static web throughput at 43.89 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 35.62 GB/sec, alongside upper-tier small-model LLM inference generation. Standard compute, memory, and database stress benchmarks perform within median industry tiers. The configuration offers favorable resource density for memory-heavy architectures, making it well fitted for Redis clusters, in-memory analytics, relational databases, and enterprise Java application tiers.
